# Bounded module authoring
Read owner instructions: ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml. Only author specs/ranges/intersection/intersection.spec.md; this is not full workflow execution.
Create it with actual installed command: npx --no-install gennady sdd-new module --scope ranges --module intersection. Read the returned manifest and skeleton; fill its sections and remove guidance.
Signature: intersectRanges(left: [number,number], right: [number,number]): [number,number] | null.
Inherited domain: Every range is an ordered pair [start,end] of finite safe integers with start <= end. Ranges are half-open: start is included and end excluded. Empty ranges start=end are valid. Validate all inputs before returning any result. No I/O or mutation.
Behavior: Return [max(left.start,right.start), min(left.end,right.end)] only when its start is strictly less than its end; otherwise return null. Touching or empty intersections are null. This entire behavior is already owned by the parent; the child introduces no new requirement.
Invalid inputs: Any non-safe-integer bound or reversed range throws TypeError, including when the other range is empty or the ranges are disjoint. Do not reorder or silently repair a reversed range.
Ownership: No new module-specific behavior: use canonical delegation to the genuine parent requirement IDs, rather than inventing local requirements.
Keep an Input/Outcome Markdown table containing all four supplied examples in MODULE_USAGE_EXAMPLE:
| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `intersectRanges([0,3],[3,6])` | `null` |
| `intersectRanges([-4,2],[-1,5])` | `[-1,2]` |
| `intersectRanges([2,2],[0,9])` | `null` |
| `intersectRanges([5,1],[0,9])` | `TypeError` |
Preserve every seeded file, parent requirement and stable identity. No implementation, new scope, tickets or operator approval. HANDOFF must explicitly remain pending-operator; no approved status or execution claim.
After the final whole-file Write, run actual npx --no-install gennady sdd-check --spec specs/ranges/intersection/intersection.spec.md --authoring. Stop after this bounded authoring task.

# Bounded module authoring
Read owner instructions: ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml. Only author specs/delivery/retry/retry.spec.md; this is not full workflow execution.
Create it with actual installed command: npx --no-install gennady sdd-new module --scope delivery --module retry. Read the returned manifest and skeleton; fill its sections and remove guidance.
Signature: shouldRetry(attempt: number, maxAttempts: number, status: number): boolean.
Inherited domain: All numeric inputs are finite safe integers. Attempts and maximum-attempt counts are positive. Times and delays are nonnegative. Validate all inputs before returning any result; never perform network I/O, wait, read a clock or mutate state.
Behavior: Return true iff (status is 429 OR status is from 500 through 599 inclusive) AND attempt < maxAttempts. Other valid statuses return false; in particular 408 is not retryable. This entire rule is already parent-owned; introduce no new child requirement.
Invalid inputs: A nonpositive/non-safe-integer attempt or maxAttempts, or a status outside the integer range 100..599, throws TypeError before deciding eligibility. attempt >= maxAttempts is valid and returns false, not an input error.
Ownership: No new module-specific behavior: use canonical delegation to the genuine parent requirement IDs, rather than inventing local requirements.
Keep an Input/Outcome Markdown table containing all four supplied examples in MODULE_USAGE_EXAMPLE:
| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `shouldRetry(1,3,503)` | `true` |
| `shouldRetry(3,3,429)` | `false` |
| `shouldRetry(1,3,408)` | `false` |
| `shouldRetry(0,3,200)` | `TypeError` |
Preserve every seeded file, parent requirement and stable identity. No implementation, new scope, tickets or operator approval. HANDOFF must explicitly remain pending-operator; no approved status or execution claim.
After the final whole-file Write, run actual npx --no-install gennady sdd-check --spec specs/delivery/retry/retry.spec.md --authoring. Stop after this bounded authoring task.

# Bounded module authoring
Read owner instructions: ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml. Only author specs/ranges/queries/contains/contains.spec.md; this is not full workflow execution.
Create it with actual installed command: npx --no-install gennady sdd-new module --scope ranges --module queries/contains. Read the returned manifest and skeleton; fill its sections and remove guidance.
Signature: containsPoint(range: [number,number], point: number): boolean.
Inherited domain: Every range is an ordered pair [start,end] of finite safe integers with start <= end. Ranges are half-open: start is included and end excluded. Empty ranges start=end are valid. Validate all inputs before returning any result. No I/O or mutation.
Behavior: New module-owned behavior: return true exactly when start <= point AND point < end. An empty range contains no point. A valid point outside the range returns false, not an exception.
Invalid inputs: An invalid range or a point that is not a finite safe integer throws TypeError, even if membership would otherwise be false.
Ownership: The behavior above is an explicit new module-owned delta; preserve parent input constraints and specify the local positive and invalid-input obligations.
Keep an Input/Outcome Markdown table containing all four supplied examples in MODULE_USAGE_EXAMPLE:
| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `containsPoint([2,5],2)` | `true` |
| `containsPoint([2,5],5)` | `false` |
| `containsPoint([2,2],2)` | `false` |

# Bounded module authoring
Read owner instructions: ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml. Only author specs/delivery/policies/dedupe/dedupe.spec.md; this is not full workflow execution.
Create it with actual installed command: npx --no-install gennady sdd-new module --scope delivery --module policies/dedupe. Read the returned manifest and skeleton; fill its sections and remove guidance.
Signature: isDuplicate(seenAtMs: number | null, nowMs: number, ttlMs: number): boolean.
Inherited domain: All numeric inputs are finite safe integers. Attempts and maximum-attempt counts are positive. Times and delays are nonnegative. Validate all inputs before returning any result; never perform network I/O, wait, read a clock or mutate state.
Behavior: New module-owned behavior: after validation, null seenAtMs returns false. Otherwise return true exactly when 0 <= nowMs-seenAtMs < ttlMs. Equality at ttl is expired; ttl=0 always yields false for valid inputs. No persistent store or clock reads.
Invalid inputs: Negative or non-safe-integer times/ttl throw TypeError. A non-null seenAtMs greater than nowMs throws TypeError, including when ttl=0. Validate nowMs and ttlMs even when seenAtMs is null.
Ownership: The behavior above is an explicit new module-owned delta; preserve parent input constraints and specify the local positive and invalid-input obligations.
Keep an Input/Outcome Markdown table containing all four supplied examples in MODULE_USAGE_EXAMPLE:
| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `isDuplicate(100,110,10)` | `false` |
| `isDuplicate(100,109,10)` | `true` |
| `isDuplicate(null,100,0)` | `false` |
| `isDuplicate(101,100,0)` | `TypeError` |
Preserve every seeded file, parent requirement and stable identity. No implementation, new scope, tickets or operator approval. HANDOFF must explicitly remain pending-operator; no approved status or execution claim.
After the final whole-file Write, run actual npx --no-install gennady sdd-check --spec specs/delivery/policies/dedupe/dedupe.spec.md --authoring. Stop after this bounded authoring task.
